eyebrow: I³/NYC Research · Ecosystem brief · Data as of October 19, 2026
title: Life sciences in the New York metro area

lede.t: A map of the region's life sciences ecosystem across New York City, Long Island, Westchester, New Jersey and southwestern Connecticut: 141 companies profiled, 42 incubators, accelerators, lab sites and public programs, 22 research institutions, and the pharma anchors around them. Built for anyone who needs to understand where the science, the money and the space are.

sub.t: Eight findings from the profiles and indicators below. Every figure is linked to its source in the sections that follow.

sub.t: The research base is the metro's deepest asset. Four New York City medical schools rank in the national top 30 for NIH funding: Columbia, NYU Langone, Mount Sinai and Weill Cornell.

caveats.t: New York City, Long Island, Westchester and the Hudson Valley, northern and central New Jersey, and Fairfield County, Connecticut. New Haven is included as adjacent because its companies and Yale are tied to the metro.

Life sciences companies headquartered in the metro, or with their primary US office here, that are public or have raised at least $1M or earned at least $1M in revenue. Acquisitions and failures since 2023 stay in with their status.

The census profiles 141 companies chosen for size, recent funding and visibility. The metro has hundreds more. Research ran against a fixed search budget; 85 names reviewed and left out are listed below with the reason.

Eight research desks (NYC therapeutics, NYC medtech and diagnostics, New Jersey and Connecticut, Long Island and Westchester, incubators and lab space, academia, ecosystem indicators, and a gap-filling pass) built lists from funding trackers, incubator portfolios, filings and trade press, and verified each record against primary or dated sources.

Company sites and releases, SEC filings, GEN, CBRE, Savills, JLL, NIH RePORTER via ConductScience, NSF HERD, Empire State Development, NJEDA, NJ Department of Labor, Fierce Biotech, Endpoints, BioSpace, NJBIZ, AlleyWatch, Bisnow. Every profile and card links its sources.
40 company profiles are rated high and 27 low. Low means the headquarters or funding rests on one aggregator or on prior knowledge. Low-confidence rows are labelled.

Founding year is missing for 84 companies and total raised for 86. Academic origin is confirmed for only 28 companies, so university spinout counts are a floor. Revenue is shown for 37 companies, mostly public ones reporting under GAAP.
Venture totals, NIH totals and job counts differ by publisher and geography. The page states the source next to each figure and does not mix them in one calculation.

On October 19, 2026 three independent reviewers re-checked 288 figures and statements against primary sources: 121 confirmed, 113 corrected and 54 could not be verified. Corrections are applied throughout; NIH figures were replaced with BRIMR's FY2025 tables, and companies checked in that pass are marked "Checked Oct 19".
Research closed October 19, 2026. Company status changes quickly: check the linked sources before acting on a record.
